utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. But you're saying that they did shoot. It is not in the indictment. Spontaneously, you said that they did shoot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they did shoot. I don't know who they shot at. I know that two people were wounded. Where the shots came from, I don't know. I was there with a few other people. I was walking around. Nobody shot at me. I did not hear a bullet whiz by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Withopf, can you please proceed. The witness is in excellent form. I believe that he can continue. If you at any point feel tired, Witness, please tell us and we shall make a break. Do you want a break now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not necessary. I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. But the Prosecution is going to be very expeditious, and we are going to gain some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I'm actually very close to finishing the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Once you were brought back to the FC Iskra Stadium in Bugojno, did the beatings continue?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was less and less beating. They saw that we weren't putting up any resistance, that we didn't want to escape, that we did good work, and then they returned us in the rain. We worked -- we walked throughout the day, and there was nowhere to get dry down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: To your knowledge, Mr. Marijanovic, did there come a time when representatives of the Red Cross visited the FC Iskra Stadium?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And do you still have a rough recollection as to when it was?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but they visited us on two occasions and brought us blankets on two occasions and jackets of some kind. Some people didn't have anything to wear. It was getting cold. But I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Was it after you came back from Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You already touched upon this issue earlier on. Who to your knowledge was in charge of the FC Iskra Stadium whilst you were detained?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew about Meho, who was a plumber. I don't know his surname. And Kukavica, who was in charge of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: This person called Meho - and I assume it's a first name - and the person called Kukavica - and I assume it's a last name - were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: They were soldiers of which army?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Marijanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, just before giving the floor to the Defence, there are a few matters I would like to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to go back to something you said earlier on in response to a question put to you by the Prosecution, that you were a member of the HVO. Does that mean that you were a member of the military or were you a civilian? What was your status within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they called me to the HVO. They said, "You're not yet 65 years old, and it is your duty to join." So there was nothing else to do. But I was more of a guard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not receiving the interpretation of what you are saying into English and into French. I would like to address the interpreters, the booths. Very well. As you were a guard, did you have a weapon? Did you have a rifle? Did you have a pistol? Or did you have insignia of any kind?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I had a rifle and a uniform. But we were on duty for one week, and then for the following week we would be free.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When you were stopped - I verified this in the transcript - when you were arrested, you said that you were in civilian clothing. So when you were arrested --

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was on leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were arrested, were you a civilian or a member of the military? In your opinion, were you a civilian at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what they thought. They knew I was a soldier. But at the time I was in civilian clothes, in short trousers, because it was summer. But as to what they thought, they never made this clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When you were in the furniture shop in which there was water -- and we have seen that a number of years later they still hadn't repaired the furniture shop, because there was still water inside. When you were in this furniture shop and your feet were in the water -- you said this very rapidly, and perhaps someone missed this, but not the Trial Chamber, that is paying particular attention to all the details. You said that there were nuns who came to provide you with food or clothes. Were these nuns aware of your detention conditions?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. They sent us oil for the lights. And if they had any food, they'd bring it. But they took more to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And apart from bringing you oil or food, what did they do? Didn't they inform the authorities of your situation, or didn't they inform their superiors of your situation? What did the nuns actually do?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that they informed someone. I don't know. I'm not sure. But everyone in Bugojno was aware of situation, and so I think that they were aware of it too. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, would you like to have a break or do you feel capable of continuing and answering further questions? Would you like to have a break now, or shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to have a short break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have a short break, a 20-minute break, which should allow you to rest. And we will resume in 20 or 25 minutes' time. Let's say that we could resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel may proceed with its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Marijanovic. My name is Edina Residovic, and I represent General Enver Hadzihasanovic. I'd be grateful if you could answer some of my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to inform you that I will ask the witness a number of questions of a general nature. I assume that the witness could answer these questions, and they are of interest for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, you have already told the Trial Chamber that you spent most of your life in Bugojno; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that in the elections immediately before the war broke out nationalist parties won in Bugojno, the HDZ obtained a majority and the SDA as the Muslim nationalist party. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was clear that in the course of the war in the Republic of Croatia the Serbian population in Bugojno and the surroundings were arming themselves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In March 1992, the Serbian forces and the JNA attacked the villages around Bugojno. They then took Kupres municipality and after that, the municipality of Donji Vakuf, not far from Bugojno. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bugojno itself, they started shelling Bugojno in May 1992; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A state of war was declared in the country and general mobilisation; isn't that correct? In May 1992, the first HVO brigade was formed in Bugojno, and its name was the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later in February 1993 another three Home Guard Battalions were formed. They formed one regiment. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't agree with that. Three battalions were established. It wasn't transferred into a regiment, because they didn't have a given number. That's how I was informed, at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But in response to a question put to you by the Trial Chamber, you said you'd been mobilised into the HVO. Were you a member of the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade or one of these newly established battalions?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the Eugen Kvaternik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, would it be correct to say that because of the wartime operations and the temporary occupation of the territory by the JNA and the Serbian forces a large number of refugees started arriving in Bugojno from Donji Vakuf and Kupres, later on from Prozor and other places; from Jajce?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: You are not going to mention Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that a large number of refugees arrived in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, since the vicinity of the combat lines -- since the combat lines were near, many of the inhabitants of Bugojno left Bugojno because they were afraid of the war and the consequence of the war. They went to the Republic of Croatia and abroad. They went to safer places. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: One could say that up until the summer of 1993 many people left, mothers and children in particular. So just before the conflict that you have mentioned broke out, about 7.000 Croats from Bugojno remained there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The majority of the refugees we have mentioned were Bosniaks. They were Muslims. So that the ethnic composition in 1993 was significantly changed; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The refugees who arrived there had in fact been expelled and they arrived there without any possessions, so this caused a big problem in Bugojno as far as accommodation and food was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in some cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in 1993 in certain areas - Vitez, Novi Travnik, and Gornji Vakuf - an open armed conflict broke out between the army and the HVO as well?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993? No, I'm not aware of that. In 1993, the HVO held the lines, because the Serbs were on Kupres. There were troops at the lines. They couldn't have started an armed conflict of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you have misunderstood me. I didn't say that that was in Bugojno. I asked you whether you were aware of the fact that in other areas, in Vitez, in Novi Travnik, in Gornji Vakuf, such conflicts broke out.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were rumours about that, but I don't know how correct they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be true to say that in 1993, given the war and the fact that the roads had been blocked, there were shortages in the town and most of the inhabitants were using aids they would get from Caritas, Merhamet, and other charities? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to a large extent, but Meho, who had a shop in Bugojno, would bring in a lot of supplies and sell them. But I don't know how he sold it. I don't know whether he was black marketeering. I don't know how much he charged for these supplies. But he had significant supplies. He had quality supplies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the population on the whole fed themselves by using aid provided by charities.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Caritas and Merhamet.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Caritas provided food. I don't know about the Merhamet charity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, would it be correct to say that before the war there was only a municipal court or a low court in Bugojno, which tried misdemeanours, but in the case of serious offences people would go to the high court or the district court in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct to say that before the war in Bugojno there was no prison where people could be sent to serve their sentences? People were sent to the KP Dom in Zenica to serve their sentences.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes? But there was the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There were basements and cells in the Bugojno police station. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But ten people at the most could be detained there; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the capacity was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be true to say that in the summer of 1993 in Bugojno and after that date there was a shortage of water?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so. I was in the centre of town, and I always had water.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps other people in other parts of the town who have testified about that had different experiences.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps. I don't know about that. All I can say is that I had water, and my neighbours did too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was while you were free; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In May 1993, there were a number of incidents and an open conflict broke out between the army and HVO units in Bugojno. This was caused by the killing of some HVO and army members, and they would capture soldiers that were members of the BH army or of the HVO, but the commanders managed to solve the problem, isn't that correct, in May?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so. Our army, the units - call it as you will - had to flee from the lines that were held in the direction of Kupres, towards the Serbian side. When they heard that the Muslims had started causing these incidents and taking over Bugojno, they had to escape. Why did the army escape from the lines?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to July 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But my question is: Did the first incidents occur in May? But they were solved, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps there were cafe skirmishes, minor skirmishes. Perhaps there were sporadic skirmishes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that on the 17th of July, at a checkpoint in the village of Vrbanja, Miroslav Talenta, an HVO member, was first killed and then three BH MUP members were killed? This conflict then spread to the entire area of Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about that, but I'm not sure. This is just a rumour I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that this conflict in the town itself lasted from the 18th of July until the 27th of July, when the last HVO stronghold in Tito's villa in Gorica was taken by the BH army? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the date, but I do remember that it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout that time, in the town and its surroundings, there was intense fighting; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you about something you have already testified about, about the period you spent in detention. You said that you were captured between the 18th and 23rd of July.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, something like that. I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just before you were captured, you were in Bozo and Iva Ivkovic's house; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your daughter and wife were in the house with you, but Mario Subasic and Vinko Ivkovic and Tomo Ivkovic were there too.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have already stated that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps previously, but you haven't mentioned this fact before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: You haven't asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I've asked you about it now, and you have answered my question. Is it true to say that Mario Subasic and Vinko Ivkovic were members of the HVO, they were members of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And Tomo, who was killed in that house, was also a member.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tomo Ivkovic was with you?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tomo Ivkovic, who died in that house, was killed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He had his own sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no one had a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mario Subasic, Tomo and Vinko had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the shooting in town, which is where you were, they shot at your house and Mario and Vinko returned fire from the house; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. You're not well informed. My house was mined, but they first opened fire on Ivkovic's house from the mosque, and then they returned fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So while this attack was carried out and fire was returned, in this exchange of fire Nuhefendic Admir a member of the army was killed. He was a well-known handball player.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what he was well known for, but I know that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the house where you were, Tomo Ivkovic was killed; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was only after that event that you, who were in the house, decided to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they forced us to do so with their shells. We had to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your daughter, you said she was 19 or 20 years old, was a medical technician --

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. You're misinformed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was she an HVO member?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: She was a secretary. She must have been a member of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So apart from your wife, all of you in the house were HVO members; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you about something else. Before the conflicts in Bugojno, the HVO wore camouflage uniforms; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: BH army members also wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were stored in the mosque. When the Mujahedin arrived, they also provided them with clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The civilian police also wore camouflage uniforms; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew some of them, and I didn't know others, because I couldn't move around Bugojno very much at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But before the conflict, throughout 1993, you saw that the HVO, the police, and the army wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the military police, but not the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, you yourself said a while ago that you have already given a statement to investigators from The Hague Tribunal. That was in the year 2000 and 2001. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. But I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to refresh the witness's memory, I would like to show him his statement, but I won't be tendering it into evidence. I have both the English and B/C/S version of the statement. And in order to be able to follow everything, I have a copy in English for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, is this the statement that you gave?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just give me a moment to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. To the Prosecutor's question, on page 26, Line 21; page 30, line 27; page 30, line 17; then page 41, line 1; page 44, line 19; page 45, line 18; page 53, line 12, you answered every time that you were arrested by the BH army, that you were beaten by the BH army, that you were guarded by the BH army, and so on and so forth. I will not repeat your words, because this is what you have stated. Can you please look at your statement now. On page 2 -- please look at your statement. The penultimate paragraph, which starts with "We all came down the stairs and surrendered to the Muslims." In the last sentence, you say: "They also had green headbands and green head scarves over their head. They had green camouflage uniforms and green ribbons." Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 2, in paragraph 6, beginning with the following words "During my stay," you said: "During my stay of two or three days in this detention facility, I didn't learn who was responsible for running it." And then in paragraph 7, you say -- actually, on page 4 -- is this what you said, is this what is written?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't learn until the moment I arrived at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So at the moment, you didn't know who was running it; is that correct? Let's move on to page 4. Open your statement on page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that page 4 in B/C/S or page 4 in English?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It's in B/C/S. That is why I'm reading the first couple of words. Page 4, paragraph 6 starts with the following words: "I heard that the Muslims used to cover the heads of the prisoners with a paper bag so that he was not able to see who were the soldiers who were beating them upstairs."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the following paragraph, it says: "When going to the toilet," the penultimate sentence says: "I can't tell you what unit the soldiers were from." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's true. They only told me that they were BH army soldiers. They never mentioned the name of their unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 6, paragraph 4, when you arrived at the stadium, third sentence says: "I didn't pay attention to their insignia because I was really scared." Is it true, Mr. Marijanovic, that in the statement that you gave earlier and that I quoted from you never mentioned that soldiers were members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I always claimed that they themselves said that they were BH army members. When I arrived at the stadium, they removed their headbands and their armbands.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, the investigator who interviewed you did not enter that fact in the statement; although, you may have told him that.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what he entered or what he didn't enter. It's not my problem, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned colleague is stating: "Is it true, Mr. Marijanovic, is that in the statement that you gave earlier and that I quoted from you never mentioned that soldiers were members of the BH army?" May I ask the witness to please read out the fourth paragraph on page 1 of his statement. Mr. Marijanovic, could you please read out the fourth paragraph on page 1 of your statement in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you please read in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have page 1. This is page 2. And I thought I was supposed to read from page 1, and this, however, is page 2 of my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is at the fourth paragraph in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stated that I was arrested by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to say to the Defence: You have told the witness that on several occasions he mentioned the army but never the BH army. We have his written statement, and it says in his written statement that in 1993 he was arrested by the BH army. I'm reading from the English version. I suppose that it is the same in the B/C/S version. Maybe he can explain why later on he never mentioned the BH army again. Maybe that would be a proper explanation. Proceed. You may continue asking your questions. I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have asked the witness as precise as that. He was arrested by the BH army, but I have quoted some other sentences from the statement about the events that he was talking about today and mentioning the BH army. But in his statement, he never mentioned the BH army. He never mentioned any of the insignia. And he never mentioned who was in charge of any of these facilities. That was the essence of my objection that I have about the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has made note of your objection, but the Prosecution has also got an observation about that. Maybe the investigator has mentioned the BH army and it was never entered in the statement. Maybe that is why the BH army is not mentioned in the rest of the sentence. But we will take this problem into account. We have taken note of your observation, and we would like to hear the position of the Prosecution. The Prosecution says that from the beginning the witness claimed in his statement that he was arrested by the BH army. Maybe Mr. Withopf would like to add something to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I would --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by my words. They kept on telling me that they were members of the BH army. I said that in my statement. And when the Prosecutor asked me about who they were, I always replied what they told me. They always told me that they were BH army members. I was not in the position to ask them questions. They asked me questions, rather than I asking them questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, would you like to intervene?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes, two issues: I again oppose any attempt by my learned colleague to state that the witness in his statement given to the OTP investigator never mentioned the BiH army. In paragraph 4, on page 1 it's absolutely clear that he made reference to the Armija BiH, and it's also clear from his B/C/S statement. In respect to the answer the witness has just given, Mr. Marijanovic, you are saying, "I stand by my words. They kept on telling me that they were members of the BiH army." Whom are you actually referring to if you say "they kept on telling me that they were members of the BiH army"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Muslims and the BH army. They were mixed. There were a lot of them from Zepa, Srebrenica. There were people whom I had never seen before. I don't know where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't understand this manner. My learned friend will be in the position to do re-examination of my examination-in-chief [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are right. The Defence will continue its cross-examination, and then you will given the floor for re-examination. The Chamber has made a note of the problem, and we'll take it into consideration. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, to the Prosecutor's question, you replied that you stayed in the grammar school for some 15 or 20 days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I also said that I was not sure about the duration of time, that it seems to me that it was between 15 and 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 33, line 4 of the transcript, you said, "10, 15, or 20 days."

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On your statement on page 3 -- look at your statement, please, page 3 of the B/C/S version, the paragraph which starts "During my two-to-three-days' stay." And after that, there is another paragraph which starts with the following words: "At about noontime on the second or third day, all the persons from my cell were taken out to the yard of the grammar school. There was a lorry there and we were all loaded onto that lorry." Is it true that the figures differ? If your testimony, you said 15 or 20 days; in your statement, you said 2 or 3 days.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: It may be different, but I stand by my words that it was between 10 and 15 days, 10 or 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 4 of your statement. In paragraph 3, you are talking about your stay in the furniture store. Earlier on today, on page 38, line 23 you said that you had stayed in the furniture store for 15 or 20 days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: It may be so. I can't remember. I'm not sure exactly. I can't be sure of the number of days. We didn't pay too much attention to days and dates. We just wanted to save our hide.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 4 of your earlier statement, paragraph 3 - I'm talking about the B/C/S version - you say: "I stayed there for three to five days. We did not receive any food from the Muslims during that period of time." Which then on page 6, paragraph 1 - can you please look at your statement - you said: "Having spent some three to five days in the furniture store, my name was called out. I went upstairs, and I was loaded onto a truck. Again, I can't tell you anything about the soldiers who were guarding us while we were being loaded onto the lorry. I was looking at the ground. Before that, several names were called out, and I believe that we were all taken out of the basement. When the lorry was full, it took us to the Iskra Stadium." Is it correct that in your statement you said that you had stayed in the furniture store for three to five days and not 15 to 20 days, as you have stated before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's easy to do the maths. You just add the days that I spent in Gornji Vakuf, in one detention unit, in another detention unit, and you will arrive at the truth of my stay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that these two statements are different? In one you say 3 to 5 days; in the other, you say 15 to 20.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Marijanovic, that while you were in the grammar school the families of some of the detainees started bringing you food? It was allowed. You shared that food.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in the grammar school. It was in the furniture store and at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the grammar school, you received bread during the two or three days that you were there, and you had water when you went to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, some received bread; some didn't. For example, I never received any bread.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in the furniture shop, in response to a question put to you by the Trial Chamber, you said that Sister Pavka and other sisters brought you oil which you used for lights. They brought you food and some clothes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were never maltreated while you were in the furniture shop; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was on one occasion while I went out to clean. But I wasn't beaten much. I wasn't maltreated much. They forced me to clean around the shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout your stay in the grammar school, the furniture shop, and the stadium, you never determined who was in charge of those prisons.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were Meho and Kukavica. How am I to find out who is in charge? Who should I find this out from? I only went out to walk around a bit and get a bit of water. There was no one I could ask about this. How would you obtain such information?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at the Iskra Stadium, your families were also allowed to bring you food; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But only after a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was also possible for you to go home with an escort or to go to see friends in order to wash or take care of other needs.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know the reasons. You don't know why I was never allowed to do this. The detainees -- if they knew that some of the detainees had rakija at home, plum brandy, then they would allow them to go home. But they would never let me go home. This was a select group that took them there. Only a chosen few went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Marijanovic, for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'd just like to point something out to the Defence. I see that in the transcript, page 72, line 17, you told the witness -- you said that Sister Pavka. But in the written statement there is no Sister Pavka. If you're asking this question, then you're referring to other documents or other information that you have. Because in the written statement he spoke about Catholic nuns, but no names appear. But you told the witness about someone called Sister Pavka. I don't know where this is from, but it's not from his written statement. So on page 72, line 17, the English transcript contains the words "Sister Pavka." You said that "Sister Pavka and other sisters brought you oil," whereas Sister Pavka isn't referred to in the written statement. So I don't know how you obtained this information, but this Sister Pavka must have appeared from somewhere. Can you clarify this matter for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it was probably the result of your question about the nuns. The previous witness mentioned this sister. I'll ask the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, was there a Sister Pavka among the nuns?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: When there was an exchange, that's when Sister Pavka turned up. When I came to Matina [phoen], that's when I heard that her name was Sister Pavka.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had you seen this sister before? Did she take down your names?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in my case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I'd like to apologise to the Trial Chamber. Because the previous witness who was also in the furniture shop also mentioned that name, most likely, and as a result, I had this sister in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is there any cross-examination for the other Defence team? Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We have no questions for this witness. Mr. Kubura is not charged with any of the incidents that this witness has given testimony about today. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is there any re-examination on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have a few questions in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, I understand you still have the B/C/S version of your statement you gave to the OTP investigator in front of you. Can you please have a look.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: I still stand by what I said, but sometimes I can forget certain things. You understand. I'm old, perhaps a little senile. This happened a long time ago, so it's possible for me to slip up sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Marijanovic, do you have page 1 of this statement in front of you? It reads on the heading "Izjava Svjedoka." It's actually page 2. And can you please read out the first sentence of the fourth paragraph, in your own language.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: "On one Sunday in June 1993 I was arrested by the BH army."

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: "I'm not able to tell the exact date that I was captured, but it was --"

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you have already mentioned this. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Cross-examined by my learned colleague, Mr. Marijanovic, you were saying that "They kept on telling me that they were members of the BiH army." It's page 69, line 22. Who are you referring to when you are saying "they kept on telling me that they were members of the BiH army"?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, mainly to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: To the Muslims who guarded and beat you and the other detainees?

utterances.speaker: MIJO MARIJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who were in the town, who opened fire, who were from the mosque and fired. They did all sorts of things. Not only the ones who guarded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And a very last question, Mr. Marijanovic: You have been detained in the Gimnazija building. You have been detained, as you informed us today, in the Slavonija Furniture Salon. And you have also been detained in the FC Iskra Stadium. For how long altogether, according to your recollection, have you been detained in all these three detention facilities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already said that it was eight months. He said that in the course of the examination-in-chief. There's no need to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has answered in respect to the FC Iskra Stadium that he was detained for eight months. The question now is a different one. I'm asking the witness for how long together he was detained in the Gimnazija building, in fact -- in the Slavonija Furniture Salon, and the FC Iskra Stadium.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in total. Witness, from the time you were arrested until your release, how much time passed? Have you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Eight months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Eight months. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Marijanovic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this concludes your examination. As the Prosecution have concluded its examination-in-chief and the Defence has also asked you a lot of questions about the context and relevant facts, the Trial Chamber has also asked you a number of questions, we would like to thank you for having testified before this Tribunal, in spite of your medical difficulties. Thank you for having made this effort and thank you for having testified about events that are certainly painful events for you to remember. We wish you a good trip home. The usher will now escort you out of the courtroom and the Victims and Witnesses Units will take care of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber notes that the witness understands foreign languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask the Prosecution about our future schedule. Apparently we don't have any witnesses for tomorrow. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can we please go in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what we'll do. Mr. Registrar, can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're back in open session now. We have dealt with all the items on the agenda. We have heard all the witnesses. We will resume on Monday at 2.15. And naturally, I invite everyone to be present at the sitting on Monday at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of February, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.43 p.m.,
